newsitem.title: UK: Analysts look to raise HSBC forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Analysts look to raise HSBC forecasts.

text.p: Banking analysts were set to increase their full year forecasts for HSBC Holdings Plc, with new estimates for pre-tax profit around the 5.2 to 5.3 billion stg mark, after the banking giant announced first half figures on Monday.
BZW banking analyst Tim Sykes said he was raising his full year forecast to just under 5.22 billion stg from 5.0 billion, with an estimate of 5.843 billion stg for 1998 after 5.674.

John Leonard, banking analyst at Salomon Brothers, said he would raise his forecast for 1997 to 5.3 billion stg from 5.1 billion previously, with earnings per share rising to 134 from 126 and dividend for the full year up to 50.5 or 51 pence per share from 47.
Other analysts, including Nick Collier of Morgan Stanley and David Townshend of Goldman Sachs also said they would raise estimates but had not completed their figures.

Townshend said the rise would not be large as he felt reasonably comfortable with his existing estimate of 5.03 billion stg, while Collier said his existing forecast of 4.974 billion stg would go up by a few percentage points.
Analysts were generally positive about the HSBC first half results and singled out its UK unit Midland Bank for special praise.
"Midland Bank was the big positive surprise," Townshend said, "where the cost line was very positive."
HSBC raised its pre-tax profit by 13 percent in sterling terms to 2.623 billion stg and its dividend by 33 percent to 20p per share -- both ahead of forecasts.
Midland's pre-tax profit jumped 27 percent to 829 million stg, with its cost to income ratio dropping to 56.1 percent from 62.3 percent at the end of last year.
"The overall results were good, particularly at Midland," said Collier. "There was a good increase in operating profit (2.4 billion stg from 2.0 billion)."
Analysts noted that HSBC had said it will find it difficult to reduce costs a great deal going forward and that improvements in cost income ratio will come largely from raising income.

"I was very impressed by the ability to generate growth, especially at Midland," Sykes said. "People found it hard to believe that they could turn Midland around when they bought it 1992, but they've done it."
HSBC shares rose sharply when the results were announced reaching a high of 2326p but later fell back to stand 36p higher at 2229.5p.
